title: Sharp Difference-in-Differences Bounds for Binary Outcomes Recorded through Imperfect Group-Specific Channels
banked_reason: D0.5 found a sound sharp ATT result at subfield tier, below the required field floor; no bounded same-topic improvement could bridge the paper-score ceiling 6.5 to 7.4.
gap_reasons: The bounded-drift sensitivity result gives only a set-image, nesting, and a sufficient saturation threshold; it must expose evaluable endpoint trajectories L(rho^s,rho^f), U(rho^s,rho^f) and define at least one named critical drift radius (rather than merely state the audit-width condition) to be a usable sensitivity deliverable.

The inference contribution remains a conservative Bonferroni construction because the score-calibrated dominance problem is left open, while practical significance is supported only by one rational example rather than an application or systematic numerical assessment.
paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a sharp ATT interval, joint compatibility test, finite Bernoulli completion, reliability polygon, endpoint-survival characterization, and exact confidence-rectangle projection. The D0.5 math panel passed after source attestation and repair of date-specific channel assumptions, but the general referee assessed only subfield novelty against the field floor. No Lean formalization was attempted; evaluable drift trajectories, a minimal critical radius, calibrated inference gains, and systematic applied evidence remain open.
tldr: Binary outcomes recorded by imperfect group-specific channels cannot be corrected cell by cell without checking whether the implied untreated post-treatment mean is a legal Bernoulli mean. At a prespecified reliability floor \(\varepsilon>0\), the paper gives a necessary-and-sufficient compatibility criterion, a two-dimensional reciprocal-reliability polygon for the time-shared model, finite causal completions, an endpoint-survival characterization against the cellwise relaxation, and exact confidence projection. Within an explicitly defined class satisfying date-specific sensitivity and false-positive moment restrictions, the bounded-drift analysis is sharp and obeys \(\mathcal I=\mathcal I_{\mathrm d}(0,0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm d}(\rho^s,\rho^f)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{cell}}\); the last inclusion becomes equality once each drift radius reaches its group-specific audit-box width, hence at \(\rho^s=\rho^f=(1,1)\). In the binary degenerate-instrument one-sided specialization, the cellwise endpoint matches the Gutknecht--Liu construction, while the shared-channel set is a sharper submodel. The score-calibrated dominance question remains open.
gap: General misclassification methods optimize over restricted channels, MondalWang2024 Proposition 4 bounds covariate-indexed latent binary-choice probabilities using bounded error rates while permitting heterogeneous misreporting, DentehKedagni2022 studies misclassification of treatment status in DiD, and discrete-outcome DiD clips cellwise counterfactual means to their support. None supplies a group-specific outcome-recording channel shared across dates, a prespecified positive reliability floor, the resulting four-cut polygon, or an endpoint-survival criterion against the cellwise relaxation.
fill: The paper gives \(\mathcal K(q;B,\varepsilon)\) and \(\mathcal I(q;B,\varepsilon)\), an if-and-only-if compatibility theorem with finite attaining laws, a necessary-and-sufficient characterization of strict endpoint improvement over \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{cell}}(q;B,\varepsilon)\), the exact fixed-box lift \(\mathcal C(\mathcal Q;B,\varepsilon)\), the separately conditioned estimated-audit set \(\mathcal C_n^{\tau}(B,\varepsilon)\), and the nested bounded-drift extension \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm d}(q;B,\varepsilon,\rho^s,\rho^f)\).
